camera.enable_notes: RTSP is disabled by default. In UniFi Protect: camera -> Settings -> Advanced -> RTSP, toggle on the quality (High/Medium/Low) you want. Each quality is an independent stream with its own token.

stream_discovery.notes: Local NVR login: POST https://<nvr-ip>/api/auth/login (username/password) -> session cookie TOKEN/UOS_TOKEN + x-csrf-token header; GET https://<nvr-ip>/proxy/protect/api/bootstrap; for the camera, pick a channel where isRtspEnabled is true and read its rtspAlias. channel id 0/1/2 = High/Medium/Low. Alternatively the user pastes the URL the Protect UI shows on enable.

streams.name: High (RTSP)
streams.notes: {address} is the NVR IP, not the camera. {stream_id} is the rtspAlias token. Preferred for phone players (force TCP transport). VERIFIED: the NVR answered RTSP OPTIONS 200 OK on 7447.

streams.name: High (RTSPS)
streams.notes: TLS + SRTP with a self-signed cert; many mobile players fail to negotiate it — offer as an opt-in, default to the 7447 rtsp stream.

covers: Live video feed (RTSP via the NVR)
local_access.summary: Live feed is fully local via the NVR's RTSP server (no Ubiquiti cloud), once RTSP is enabled per-camera in Protect. Camera settings/PTZ are out of scope.

device.name: Ubiquiti UniFi Protect Camera
device.notes:
UniFi Protect cameras (UVC G3/G4/G5/G6 family, AI series, and the G4/G5 Doorbell) are adopted to a UniFi Protect NVR (a UNVR, UDM-Pro, or Cloud Key Gen2+). We DISCOVER them with the Ubiquiti UDP-10001 protocol (same as ubiquiti-unifi-device.yaml — a camera answers with platform 0x0c like "UVC G4 Pro"), and we can SHOW A LIVE FEED with no Ubiquiti cloud — but the stream is served by the NVR, not the camera, and RTSP is OFF by default.
FEED (see the `camera` block): - RTSP must be ENABLED per-camera, per-quality (High/Medium/Low) in the
  UniFi Protect UI. Until then no stream token exists.
- Once enabled, the stream lives on the NVR at
  rtsp://<nvr-ip>:7447/<streamId>  (plaintext) or
  rtsps://<nvr-ip>:7441/<streamId>?enableSrtp  (TLS+SRTP). The <streamId>
  (rtspAlias) is an opaque per-quality token that IS the secret — no
  username/password on the RTSP URL. Prefer plain 7447 for phone players:
  Protect's rtsps uses SRTP + a self-signed cert that most mobile players
  (ffmpeg/libVLC) fail to negotiate, while 7447 plays reliably (force TCP
  transport; e.g. media_kit on Flutter).
- Getting the token programmatically (optional): log in to the NVR locally
  (POST https://<nvr-ip>/api/auth/login -> TOKEN/UOS_TOKEN cookie +
  x-csrf-token header), GET https://<nvr-ip>/proxy/protect/api/bootstrap,
  and read cameras[].channels[] for isRtspEnabled + rtspAlias. Or just let
  the user paste the URL the Protect UI shows when they enable RTSP.

The NVR is discovered as a separate device (platform "UNVR"/"UDM"/"UCKP" via the same UDP-10001 sweep); a consumer pairs a camera to its NVR to build the feed host. Camera control (PTZ, settings) is out of scope — this entry is feed + identity only.
Admin: https://<nvr-ip>/ (UniFi OS -> Protect). A camera's own page is https://<camera-ip>/ before adoption.

credentials.notes: The RTSP token IS the feed secret (no user/pass on the URL). To fetch it programmatically the app authenticates to the NVR with a LOCAL UniFi OS account (session cookie + CSRF), which the user supplies — no cloud.
stored_on_device: The per-quality RTSP stream token (rtspAlias), created when RTSP is enabled

factory_reset.effect: Done at the camera (reset button) and re-adopted in UniFi Protect; clears the camera's own adoption, not anything this app stores. We only read the feed.

methods.description: Camera is adopted to a Protect NVR on the LAN; discovery is the UDP-10001 probe, feed is RTSP from the NVR.

steps.action: Broadcast the Ubiquiti v1 probe 01 00 00 00 to UDP 10001; a camera answers with platform (e.g. 'UVC G4 Pro') and hostname.
Enable RTSP for the camera (per quality) in the UniFi Protect UI.
Obtain the streamId (paste the Protect-shown URL, or fetch cameras[].channels[].rtspAlias from the NVR bootstrap after a local login) and play rtsp://<nvr-ip>:7447/<streamId>.
steps.expect: The NVR's RTSP server (Server: Media Server (www.ui.com)) serves the H.264 stream.

setup.notes: Discovery needs nothing (UDP-10001 probe). To view a feed the user enables RTSP for the camera in UniFi Protect once; after that the app plays rtsp://<nvr>:7447/<streamId>. Confidence high for discovery and the transport (both verified live); the credentialed token fetch is documented from the RE'd local API but not exercised here.

rejoin.notes: Camera stays discoverable by the UDP-10001 probe; the feed follows the NVR, so a camera IP change does not change the stream URL (the NVR host + rtspAlias do). Identity keys on MAC/hostname.

testing.notes: Discovery + feed transport verified live 2026-08-14. Ubiquiti discovery (UDP 10001) enumerated the whole camera fleet by model — UVC G3 Dome ("Creeper cam"), UVC AI 360, UVC G4 Pro ("Fence Cam"/"yard"/"Roof Cam"), UVC G4 Dome ("garage inside"), UVC G6 Bullet, UVC G4 PTZ, UVC G3 Instant and a UVC G4 Doorbell ("G4 Doorbell") — each via platform (0x0c) and hostname (0x0b) TLVs. The feed transport was confirmed on the UNVR ("UNVR-holden"): RTSP port 7447 and RTSPS 7441 are open, and an RTSP OPTIONS to 7447 answered "RTSP/1.0 200 OK ... Server: Media Server (www.ui.com)" advertising DESCRIBE/PLAY/SETUP — i.e. the Protect stream server is live and serving. NOT exercised (no local Protect credentials were used): the bootstrap login that yields a camera's rtspAlias token, and playing an actual stream (which additionally needs RTSP enabled per-camera in the Protect UI).
